comment: Which committed artifact each `content_hash` in block-manifest.json pins.
Every citation the manifest makes must add its entry here in the same PR:
klt compares a manifest pin against the *cited envelope's own*
provenance.input.content_hash -- it never looks at the repo file the hash
is supposed to be the hash *of*. So a pin can go stale in two independent
ways, and only one of them is klt's business:
1. the cited envelope ran against a different revision than the pin
(klt catches this: reason `stale_evidence`), and
2. the pinned artifact itself changed in the repo since the pin was
written, so the pin no longer describes current sources at all
(klt cannot catch this -- it never reads the artifact).
This file closes (2): signoff/check_signoff.py re-hashes every path below
and fails when it no longer equals the manifest's pin for that item. It is
stdlib-only and PDK-free, so it runs in the offline half of the CI
signoff job with no klt and no network -- see signoff/README.md.

Items 2, 3 and 4 pin the *same* artifact on purpose. 2 and 3 cite the
        one `klt drc` envelope over layout/opamp_core/opamp_core.gds, and 4
        cites the `klt lvs` envelope over the same stream; both envelope kinds
        record the sha256 of the layout they ran on (`provenance.input`) -- so
        the pin is the committed GDS's own hash in all three cases, and the
        re-hash here is what turns "the envelope says it ran on this hash"
        into "and that hash is the layout committed in this repo".
        Regenerating the layout therefore fails the offline check until the
        DRC report, the LVS report and all three pins are refreshed together.
`klt drc` envelope over layout/opamp_core/opamp_core.gds, and a DRC
envelope records the sha256 of the stream it ran on -- so the pin is the
committed GDS's own hash in both cases, and the re-hash here is what turns
"the envelope says it ran on this hash" into "and that hash is the layout
committed in this repo". Regenerating the layout therefore fails the
offline check until the DRC report and both pins are refreshed together.
Item 11 is the one COMPOUND citation (klayout-tools#2025): power
delivery (structural) is not proved by a single artifact, so the
manifest cites a *list* -- the `klt erc` supply run
(layout/opamp_core/erc_report.json, against the supply spec
layout/opamp_core/erc_supply_spec.json) plus the same `klt lvs`
envelope item 4 cites. Its entry below is therefore a list too, one
artifact per part in the same order, and check_signoff.py re-hashes
each part's own pin. Both parts land on the same GDS hash for the same
reason items 2/3/4 do -- an `erc` envelope records the sha256 of the
stream it ran on in `provenance.input`, exactly as `drc` and `lvs` do.
Note what this does NOT pin: the ERC *spec document* is named by the
envelope (`spec`) and hashed by newer klt in `provenance.spec`, but the
revision pinned in klt-pin.txt predates that check, so editing the
supply spec without re-running layout/opamp_core/run_erc.sh would not
be caught here. Re-run it whenever the spec changes.
